newsitem.title: USA: Jan cash flow to U.S. stock funds $29.39 bln-ICI.
newsitem.headline: Jan cash flow to U.S. stock funds $29.39 bln-ICI.

text.p: U.S. stock mutual funds received net new cash inflows of $29.39 billion in January, the Investment Company Institute reported Thursday.

That was a new record for January, greater than the $28.9 billion inflow to stock funds seen at the start of last year and well up from the estimated figure of $24 billion released by the industry trade group over two weeks ago.
The January inflows to stock funds compared to $11.75 billion in December.

"January's inflow to stock funds relects, among other things, seasonal influences related to retirement account activity and the investment of year-end bonuses," ICI deputy chief economist Mitchell Post said.
ICI said bond and income funds had inflows of $2.94 billion in January compared to $2.35 billion in December and $4.28 billion a year earlier.
Money market funds had inflows of $21.15 billion in January, compared with $3.53 billion in December and $23.93 billion in January last year.
